summary: Unexpected prefetch backpressure from multi-tenant aggregation causing dedicated pool throughput collapse
description:
Issue summary:
During a midday traffic shift on 2026-03-10 the ClearSight dedicated capacity pool (prod/us-west) experienced a sharp p99 latency increase and a sustained throughput fall (~40%) for ~90 minutes. Surface symptoms pointed to slow GPU attach and long batch serialization times.

Impact:
- Customer ClearSight (dedicated) reported increased inference timeouts and elevated error rates for RW-infer-13B and RW-infer-7B routes.
- Estimated request drop / retry rate increased by ~18% for the tenant window.
- Business impact: degraded user-facing features for ClearSight (reporting dashboards), impacting SLAs.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: prod/us-west, reserved capacity (8 GPUs)
- Affected models: rw-infer-13b, rw-infer-7b
- Redwood platform components: serving-runtime v2.8.1, autoscaler v1.4.0, prefetch-aggregator v0.9.2

Steps to reproduce / observed behavior:
1) Run steady small-stream workload against ClearSight pinned model routes (peak window ~11:45-13:30 UTC).
2) Observe that new connections stall at "attaching GPU slot" for 200-600ms longer than baseline; batches serialize more often (single-request batches spike).
3) Datadog dashboards show prefetch-aggregator queue length growth and a sharp increase in kv-cache eviction rate.

Relevant logs / metrics (excerpts):
- scheduler logs: "attach_latency_ms p50=12 p90=48 p99=410"
- prefetch-aggregator: "queue_size=172 -> 1.6k in 12m; backpressure=true; upstream_time_ms=380"
- gpu allocator: "attach_retry=3; attach_error=OOM? false; attach_backoff_ms=500"
- serving-runtime traces: repeated tiny batches, KV cache miss rate +42%

Initial investigation notes:
- Hypothesis 1: A tenant (ClearSight) sent many small long-lived streams that increased prefetch-aggregator aggregation latency and caused starvation of pooled batchers.
- Hypothesis 2: Prefetch aggregator aggregated metadata across tenants causing head-of-line blocking when one tenant's streams stalled (noisy neighbor pattern).
- Hypothesis 3: Autoscaler telemetry read aggregated attach latencies and interpreted the signal as transient, avoiding scale-up.

What we checked so far:
- Correlated Datadog traces with allocator metrics; found sustained increase in prefetch-aggregator processing latency coincident with kv-cache evictions.
- Inspected prefetch-aggregator host list: one host reported periodic GC pauses (container-level OOM-kill events seen in host metrics) at the same time as queue growth.
- Looked at tenant request profiles: ClearSight had a high fraction of tiny, high-concurrency short streams during the window.

Mitigation taken (temporary):
- Isolated ClearSight traffic onto a dedicated subpool within the reserved cluster (manual routing) at 2026-03-10 12:05 UTC. This removed cross-tenant aggregation and restored baseline throughput within ~7 minutes.
- Restarted two prefetch-aggregator replicas and applied a temporary per-tenant queue cap (config flag) to limit head-of-line blocking.

Current status and next steps:
- Root cause inspection ongoing. Priority is to: (A) reproduce in staging with a synthetic mix of many small streams + induced host GC pauses, (B) instrument prefetch-aggregator to expose per-tenant processing time and queue metrics, and (C) evaluate autoscaler sensitivity to attach-latency signals so it scales appropriately instead of ignoring transient but sustained backpressure.
- Proposed short-term fix: enforce per-tenant queue limits in prefetch-aggregator and add a backpressure signal for autoscaler to consider aggregated prefetch queue depth.
- Longer-term follow-up: improve tenant isolation in scheduling and consider preferring per-tenant batching windows to prevent cross-tenant head-of-line effects.

Attachments / links:
- Datadog graph: https://app.datadog.com/graph/abcd-prefetch-queue
- Allocator trace: https://logs.redwood/infer/alloc/2026-03-10/attach-trace-xyz

Requested from Engineering/SRE:
- SRE: validate host-level GC and container memory settings for prefetch-aggregator hosts (INT-4420 linked).
- Serving Runtime: add lightweight per-tenant metrics to prefetch-aggregator (PR referenced below).

Resolution (temporary):
- Manual tenant isolation restored customer throughput and met immediate SLA obligations. Root-cause engineering work continues.
